newsitem.title: UK: KAL axes ex-Europe cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: KAL axes ex-Europe cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: Korean Air Lines said it would drop its ex-Europe cargo fuel surcharge equivalent to 10 U.S. cents a kg from April 21.
UK cargo manager Frank Smith said the carrier applied surcharges on flights from Europe last November 1, following the lead of Lufthansa Cargo AG and other carriers.
As Lufthansa announced it would abolish its cargo fuel surcharges from April 15, Korean quickly decided to do the same from Germany and other Continental Europe markets.
"From the UK, where our surcharge is six pence per kg, I was waiting to see what British Airways would do about the situation before taking any action here," Smith told Reuters.
"But even though BA has made no announcement as yet, most other airlines have decided to drop their surcharges and so we are going to do the same," he said.
He said that apart from Europe, Korean did not apply cargo fuel surcharges in other markets around the world.
